sources.projection: Agent reliability depends materially on the execution harness and benefits from observability that links predictions, runtime events and outcomes rather than treating the model alone as the unit of engineering.
rakl_mapping: bind model proposal execution to explicit runtime events and outcomes
future provider adapters should expose enough trace state to localize model versus harness failures
sources.novelty_effect: observability-driven harness engineering is prior art

sources.projection: Distributed execution observability is represented with traces/spans carrying timing, attributes, status, resources and causal parentage.
rakl_mapping: RAKL execution events/receipts should have stable identities and timing suitable for later trace export
telemetry representation does not grant scientific truth authority
sources.novelty_effect: trace/span observability semantics are established standards

sources.projection: subprocess.run provides explicit argv, stdin/stdout/stderr capture, environment and timeout behavior; shell invocation has separate security semantics.
rakl_mapping: local provider runner uses argv sequence with shell=False
timeout/start/nonzero failures remain distinct execution states
sources.novelty_effect: safe subprocess execution and timeout semantics are standard-library prior art

sources.source: LangGraph persistence and durable execution documentation
sources.projection: Checkpointed execution preserves graph state and pending writes for durable recovery and avoids indiscriminate reruns of completed work.
rakl_mapping: terminal RAKL invocation receipts replay without duplicate execution
ambiguous side-effecting states should fail closed rather than restart blindly
sources.novelty_effect: durable checkpoint/recovery architecture is prior art

remaining_rakl_specific_question: Whether binding these execution controls to RAKL's proposal-only epistemic authority, exact task-packet provenance, immutable negative history and separately governed promotion measurably reduces scientific-process failure versus matched agent runtimes.
